mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized articles of association (statuts) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentic deed issued by Luxembourg notary; Hague Apostille only if the notarial deed must be transmitted abroad for foreign corporate or tax filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residence of each shareholder, director and key compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for all issuing countries party to the 1961 Hague Convention; Consular Legalization for non-contracting states; certified French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of address / lease agreement or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Landlord or approved Luxembourg domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-origin documents; French translation required if not in French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal bank certificate; notarized confirmation used for the notarial deed; no apostille required for domestic use

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC identification of all natural-person shareholders and beneficial owners; mandatory screening against UN, EU, OFAC and Luxembourg domestic sanctions lists; mandatory PEP categorization for politically exposed persons and enhanced due diligence; continuous and event-triggered re-screening required under CSSF-CRF guidance and Luxembourg AML/CFT law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyLBR portal (lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be single and identifiable, must not violate public order, must not be misleading, must be in Latin script and transliterated as necessary into French for official registration; the legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS notifies the applicant of name rejection; the applicant may submit a corrective name application or file an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months from notification; the applicant may alternatively request an extension of reservation before expiry if a notarial deed is already drafted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office must be a real and exact Luxembourg address; a commercial domiciliation agent may be used if the arrangement provides physical presence and access to the SARL's records. A purely virtual office without local substance is not accepted for SARL incorporation. For an AI/LLM API platform, a professional domiciliation agreement is permissible, but the substance requirements for tax and AML purposes must be satisfied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for this industry: approximately 5% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax or social security authorities; higher inspection risk may apply where the domiciliation address is shared, records are not maintained locally, or the SARL does not have identifiable commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated; SARL provisions under Articles 180 to 185-1 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); Law of 2 September 2011 on the Business Establishment Permit
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), acting jointly with a Luxembourg civil-law notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte de constitution) embodying the Articles of Association (Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital for a standard SARL, fully subscribed and fully paid up at formation; the capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution and confirmed by a bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) delivered to the notary prior to execution of the deed; the alternative EUR 1 capital regime is available only for micro-enterprises and subject to statutory payment restrictions
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [•] S.À R.L. The sole shareholder hereby resolves: (1) to approve and adopt the Articles of Association executed before a Luxembourg civil-law notary on [•]; (2) to ratify the subscription and full payment of the issued share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 12,000 shares with a par value of EUR 1.00 each, evidenced by the bank blocking certificate issued by [Bank]; (3) to fix the registered office at [Street, L-•••• City], Luxembourg; (4) to appoint [•] and [•] as managers (gérants) holding joint signature authority; (5) to authorize the managers to execute the RCS filing, RESA publication, business establishment permit application, VAT registration, social security enrollment, and all ancillary formalities; and (6) to ratify all pre-incorporation acts. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Check and Drafting of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary in consultation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); name pre-check against the RCS electronic index
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to conduct a name availability search on the RCS electronic index and to draft the articles of association in French or German; verify the ISIC 6201 scope (generative AI and LLM API services), the share structure of 12,000 shares at EUR 1.00 each, the registered office clause, and the manager provisions; collect identity documents and criminal record certificates of all shareholders and managers to support the notary's due diligence; deliver the final draft statutes to the subscribing shareholders for approval before signature.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all shareholders and managers
Certificate of no criminal record (casier judiciaire) for each manager
Proof of residential address of shareholders and managers
Name availability confirmation issued from the RCS index
Draft articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed corporate name is refused by the RCS index check, the notary submits alternative name options and the articles of association are amended accordingly before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Deposit of EUR 12,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) selected by the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the company in formation; deposit the full share capital of EUR 12,000 in cash; provide complete KYC documentation and source-of-funds evidence to the bank; instruct the bank to issue a capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, confirming the account holder, the deposited amount, and the irrevocable blocking condition until the RCS registration extract is presented; the certificate must be delivered before the notarial deed is executed.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application form
Draft articles of association
KYC documents and source-of-funds declaration for all shareholders
Beneficial ownership statement (registers des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Bank capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, supply supplementary bank statements or asset origin evidence within 10 business days; if the account request is ultimately declined, select an alternative credit institution and re-deposit the capital with a new blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive meeting at the notary's office; all shareholders or their duly authorized attorneys-in-fact must appear for simultaneous execution; the notary verifies the blocking certificate, reads the articles of association in full, and authenticates the signatures; each manager must deliver a written acceptance of office and a declaration of no ineligibility; the deed is read, approved, and signed before the notary, who then assumes responsibility for the subsequent RCS electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Approved draft articles of association
Bank capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Written acceptance of office by each manager
Declaration on honour of no ineligibility (déclaration sur l'honneur)
Notarized power of attorney if a shareholder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires rectification of statutory clauses, correct the deficient provisions in the draft and re-execute the deed; if a power of attorney is challenged, the represented shareholder must appear personally before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the incorporation deed electronically with the RCS within one month of signature; the RCS reviews the legality, enters the company in the register, and assigns the RCS number and LEI identifier, at which point the company acquires legal personality; the deed and coordinating extracts are published in the RESA electronic collection; obtain the RCS registration extract (extrait) and the LEI code from the LBR portal for subsequent bank and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (transmitted electronically by the notary)
RCS registration application form
Statement of subscribed and fully paid-up capital
Registered office consent form signed by the landlord
RCS filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (examen), the notary submits corrected documentation within the statutory deadline; if publication is suspended, rectify the administrative mistakes and refile; any refusal may be appealed before the District Court of Luxembourg in summary proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit, VAT, Social Security, and Data Protection Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (via guichet.lu single window); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS); National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the business establishment permit application (autorisation d'établissement) on guichet.lu within three months of actual commencement, proving professional integrity and suitable premises; register for VAT with the AEDT; enroll the managers and employees with the CCSS for social security; file the data processing register with the CNPD covering the AI API platform's handling of personal data; maintain the RCS extract, permit, and supporting records at the registered office for inspection.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Business establishment permit application filed via guichet.lu
Criminal record certificate of each manager
VAT registration form submitted to the AEDT
CNPD data processing notification
CCSS employer registration form
Lease agreement or proof of premises title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal of the business establishment permit may be appealed to the Minister of the Economy within three months of notification and thereafter to the administrative courts; VAT or social security compliance queries are cured by filing the outstanding declarations within the deadlines stated in the AEDT or CCSS correspondence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Middle Office for Business Establishment (autorisation d'établissement), administered through the guichet.lu single window
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) for commercial and IT/AI service activities under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Registration/Exempt: office-based generative AI and LLM API platform with no industrial installations; no full EIA required under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; a simple environmental declaration may be filed if dedicated server rooms are installed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing wastewater or VOC emissions; any sanitary wastewater must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation on municipal wastewater discharge; IT hardware must be disposed of under Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE) and Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS); standby generators, if installed, must comply with EU Regulation 2016/1628 emission limits; data center and server operations should follow the EU Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the Luxembourg premises issued by the CGDIS (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours); structural load inspection for the server and IT equipment room; workplace safety inspection and risk assessment under the ITM (Inspection du travail et des mines); electrical installation conformity certificate for the registered office

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg (www.impotsdirects.public.lu). VAT: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg (www.aedt.public.lu). Customs: Administration des douanes et accises (ADA). Unified taxpayer portal and e-filing: www.myguichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP: (1) file the notarised deed of incorporation with Luxembourg Business Registers (www.lbr.lu) to obtain the 11-digit national identification number (matricule d'identification); (2) after RCS registration, file VAT registration form (form 176/F/3 or myguichet.lu eDesk application) with the AEDT within 15 days of commencing taxable activity, receiving a LU + 8-digit VAT identification number; (3) ACD corporate income tax file is opened automatically upon RCS registration, and notices are issued to the registered office; (4) a non-resident entity supplying B2B/B2C digital services into Luxembourg without an establishment may register directly under the OSS/IOSS or standard VAT registration, and a tax representative is required only where no EU establishment exists and special regimes so prescribe.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Luxembourg-resident SARL is fully taxable on worldwide profits: corporate income tax 17% + 7% solidarity surcharge (effective 18.19%) + municipal business tax of approx. 6.75% (Luxembourg City) = aggregate headline rate approx. 24.94%. Participation exemption fully exempts qualifying dividends (100%) and capital gains (100%) on qualifying shareholdings; foreign PE profits are exempt under treaty/PE exemption. SARL is not a pass-through entity; no fiscal transparency applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Mandatory entity-level taxation unless an entity opts into, or satisfies the conditions of: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for CIT and municipal business tax requiring a direct or indirect holding of at least 95% for a continuous 5-year commitment; (2) VAT group election (assujetti unique) for persons established in Luxembourg; (3) option to treat certain transparent partnerships as CIT taxpayers under Art. 172bis LIR (not applicable to an SARL); (4) EU ATAD hybrid mismatch neutralisation rules apply (Directives 2016/1164 and 2017/952) without elective repatriation, and the IP box election (80% exemption) is available for qualifying IP income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-resident suppliers: EUR 0 (no threshold; any taxable supply of digital services in Luxembourg triggers VAT registration unless covered by OSS/IOSS). Domestic SME exemption: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (Art. 57 VAT Law). Intra-EU distance sales of goods: EUR 100,000 EU-wide annual threshold; imports of goods in consignments not exceeding EUR 150: IOSS. Mandatory registration applies for B2C telecommunication, broadcasting and e-services irrespective of turnover when the customer is established in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing through the PEPPOL network applies from 1 January 2023 for public sector supplies; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, with EDI and structured e-invoice formats accepted. VAT returns are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu on a monthly or quarterly basis; intra-EU recapitulative statements (ESL) are filed monthly; OSS and IOSS returns are filed quarterly through the national portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to (a) export of goods to destinations outside the EU, evidenced by transport documents leaving the customs territory of the Union; (b) intra-EU B2B supplies of digital services subject to reverse charge; (c) B2B services to non-EU business customers where place of supply is outside Luxembourg; (d) B2C digital services to consumers outside the EU and outside the Union VAT area, which fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope. For AI/LLM API platform services supplied B2B to EU customers, the reverse charge applies (place of supply at customer location); for B2C EU customers, VAT applies at 17% via OSS. No statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline is codified in Luxembourg law; the 180-day convention reflects prudent OECD transfer-pricing practice and standard commercial invoice terms.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Single Administrative Document) accepted and cleared by Luxembourg Customs (ADA) or another EU customs office of export
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Export accompanying document (EAD) and transport contract
Proof of payment and, where applicable, Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT confirmation of receipt in EUR/USDC
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may claw back unjustified zero rating within a 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, wilful default or material irregularity (Art. 114 VAT Law). Deliberate VAT fraud is punishable by fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years (Art. 248 VAT Law; Art. 396 LIR); negligent or incorrect filing triggers surcharges from 10% to 200% of the tax due. Customs export fraud penalties reach EUR 250,000 per material false declaration. Supporting customs, transport and invoicing records must be retained for at least 5 years, or 10 years where fraud is suspected.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); in the context of the Eurosystem, the European Central Bank (ECB) exercises supranational monetary authority for the eurozone, including Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully integrated member of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). The euro is freely convertible on both current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls or restrictions on capital movements under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the Luxembourg Law of 11 January 2008 implementing EU free movement of capital provisions. Profit remittance is generally unrestricted; dividends may be freely distributed subject to the Luxembourg SARL's articles of association, the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended, and compliant corporate formalities (e.g., approval of annual accounts by the shareholders' meeting and clearance of the corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax arrears). There are no convertibility hurdles for resident or non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg and the eurozone have no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts, and no requirement to repatriate proceeds to a specific local bank account. All receipts may be held in EUR or any freely convertible currency in accordance with standard treasury policy.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Client Sub-Accounts
Capital Escrow Account / Wealth Management Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to medium viability. Luxembourg-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and may offer local IBANs, but most established EMIs focus on payment services rather than complex corporate treasury cash management. Offshore digital EMIs (non-EU/EEA licensed, e.g., from the UK or the British Virgin Islands) cannot legally provide payment services to Luxembourg entities without an EU/EEA passport. Such EMIs may be used only in limited, non-prudential areas (e.g., receivable collection) but are not recommended as primary clearing rails for a regulated SARL due to EU passporting constraints and CSSF compliance expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SARL, there is no statutory mandate that all directors appear physically in front of a bank representative. In practice, the CSSF’s anti-money laundering (AML) regime demands that the bank identify the beneficial owner(s) and senior managing directors. Remote opening is permitted via video identification, but the bank may require the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to attend an in-person interview if the risk profile is elevated, the company's activities are complex, or the onboarding application includes payment rails such as cryptocurrency (USDC) that require enhanced due diligence. A physical presence, or at least a virtual meeting with a Luxembourg-based notary or a regulated lawyer, significantly increases onboarding success at Tier-1 banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with no Luxembourg banking history and no established EU economic nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract (RCS) dated within 3 months; beneficial ownership register (RBE) extract; notarised articles of association; an affidavit from the UBO explaining source of funds, source of wealth, and a detailed group structure chart; audited (or, if not audited, management-prepared) financial statements of the SARL; a Luxembourg VAT certificate and trade licence (if applicable); utility bill or lease agreement for a registered office in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business plan includes accepting cryptocurrency (USDC) as a payment rail for AI/LLM API platform tokens
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive AML/CFT risk assessment and policies & procedures for crypto-to-fiat conversions; a compliance framework demonstrating the use of a licensed EU crypto-asset service provider (under MiCA regime, when applicable); details of the wallet architecture and transaction monitoring; a declaration that the company does not facilitate money laundering or terrorist financing; complete UBO structure with clear source of crypto funds; an independent legal opinion on the tax and legal treatment of USDC in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Long gap between incorporation and account opening; no prior operational transaction history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised board resolution provided by the directors; an audited business plan with revenue projections and product description; signed client/partner contracts or Letters of Intent (LOIs) evidencing genuine commercial substance; a detailed transaction flow forecast for the first 6–12 months; evidence that the entity will comply with Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax filing obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity or shareholder loan transfers to a Luxembourg SARL should be executed through the SWIFT network (MT103) or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR. The payment must include the following purpose code (SWIFT category) and remittance information: for equity injection, use 'EQUI' (
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.Equity Injection): For inbound equity injection, use the SWIFT purpose code 'EQUI' (capital contribution) or a specific EU Balance of Payments (BoP) code 'D311' (equity capital). For a shareholder loan, use 'D322' (intercompany loan) or SWIFT purpose code 'INTL'. The remittance field 'Purpose of Payment' must explicitly state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – SARL LU_SARL' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN – LU_SARL' and must reference the company’s Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) 549300LUX and the registered office address. The bank will require a copy of the executed shareholders' subscription agreement, the notarised capital contribution deed (or bank confirmation of subscribed capital), and a board resolution confirming the capital entry. For amounts above EUR 10,000, the bank will report the transaction to the Luxembourg Central Bank (BCL) for statistical BoP purposes. For USDC inbound conversion into EUR, the conversion must be executed through a licensed crypto-to-fiat intermediary (CASP) that complies with Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA) and the CSSF Circular 22/806 (if applicable).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements (e.g., subcontractor invoices, licensing fees, cloud infrastructure costs, employee payroll) should use exact-value Euro payments via the TARGET2 / SEPA rail for EU counterparties, or a SWIFT MT103 for non-EU counterparties. For commercial letters of credit (L/C) operations, Luxembourg banks typically issue irrevocable documentary credits subject to UCP 600 (ICC Publication No. 600). If the SARL is an exporter, it may be the beneficiary under a confirmed L/C; for importers, the bank will handle issuance and negotiation. All outgoing payments must identify the beneficiary bank BIC, beneficiary IBAN, and the remittance field referencing the underlying invoice number and VAT identification number (LU...). For payments to non-EU countries, the MT103 field 57A (Account With Institution) and field 70 (Remittance Information) must contain the correct purpose code (e.g., 'D920' for telecommunications services, 'D890' for data processing services) and the reference to the AI/LLM API licensing agreement. Separation of trust or escrow funds: the SARL should maintain a distinct client funds / operational account to avoid commingling, and subscribe to the Luxembourg CSSF circular on virtual currency (Circular CSSF 20/719) if any part of the crypto payment rail is used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Forward (deliverable via CLS or onshore banking channel)

EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for non-convertible or notional hedging of USDC receivables (though NDFs are generally not required for euro because EUR is freely convertible; still available with major banks)
EUR/USD Cross-Currency Swap (fixed-for-floating and fixed-for-fixed, with appropriate MTM collateral agreement under ISDA/CSA)
EUR/USD Currency Option (European-style vanilla options for risk management only)
EUR/SDR or EUR/CHF forward contracts for multi-currency liquidity buffers
Perpetual Swaps (synthetic FX) through regulated EU exchanges or banks only; cryptocurrency-denominated derivatives are permitted only if executed on an EU-regulated venue under MiCA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; certifies that the previously filed UBO data remains complete and accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal RBE registrar notice; continued non-confirmation triggers criminal fines under the Law of 13 January 2019 and possible public prosecution of directors; substantially delayed confirmation may block shareholder distributions and request for official corporate extracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return covering corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via MyGuichet / GeCo tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end SARL, due 31 May of the following year; the tax administration routinely grants an extension to 30 June for electronic filings and may grant further extension on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; late payment interest of 0.6% per month; failure to file allows the tax office to issue an estimated assessment and opens the file to audit scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS), including balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, management report, and auditor's report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December SARL, no later than 31 July; shareholder approval of annual accounts must occur within 6 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS sends formal notice; continued non-filing may lead to court-ordered filing with daily penalty payments, criminal fines on directors up to EUR 5,000, civil director liability, and, for dormant companies, judicial strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds two of three thresholds at the balance sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average 25 employees. Below these thresholds the SARL is exempt from mandatory audit unless required by its articles of association, by shareholder request, or by parent-entity obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Luxembourg accounting standards framework; IFRS is optional for unlisted statutory accounts and mandatory for listed consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE annual confirmation is due each calendar year by 31 March. A share transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be filed separately within one month of the transaction; the annual confirmation does not replace this immediate update. Before confirming, the compliance officer must reconcile the Register of Members, share transfer records, RBE filings, and any pledges or restrictions to ensure the disclosed UBO structure is current and accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,500 (approximate annual fee for registered office and registered agent services in Luxembourg)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - 18,000 for a small to mid-sized SARL under Luxembourg GAAP; the lower end applies to companies at or below the audit exemption thresholds where a review or agreed-upon procedures may suffice.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (IRC); combined Luxembourg City statutory burden 22.80% including 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax; effective rate approx. 21.72% after deduction of municipal tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; preferential regimes include 80% IP-box exemption on qualifying IP income, enhanced R&D tax credit of 20% on eligible expenses, investment tax credit for digital/efficient assets, participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, and reduction of taxable base through group relief/consolidation mechanisms where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the Luxembourg e-filing portal MyGuichet.lu; municipal business tax is reported via the same annual declaration; net wealth tax is filed separately on Form 547.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; advance payments of the final corporate income tax liability are due quarterly on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the current fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 100 must be filed within twelve months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 31 December of the following year; later extensions may be granted on request to the Luxembourg tax administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the taxpayer: legal name, registered office, RCS number, Luxembourg tax number, VAT number, accounting period opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL is resident as entity level; the non-resident parent/shareholder is irrelevant at this box unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment is declared separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory accounting profit before tax, prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in EUR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Embed the full AI/LLM API revenue into the Luxembourg company accounts. No revenue can be diverted to non-resident shareholders without correct transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: disallowable expenses, participation exemption, IP-box deduction, R&D credit, loss carryforward utilisation, interest limitation adjustments, and transfer-pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related-party invoices, IP royalty payments, and crypto/USDC conversion fees must be documented at arm's length; absence of evidence triggers reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax after deducting prepayments and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any resulting liability is payable in EUR by bank transfer; non-payment triggers enforcement against the Luxembourg corporate assets and, where applicable, directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a procedural fine up to EUR 5,000, a monthly late-payment surcharge of 0.5% on unpaid tax up to 20%, and 2.6% annual default interest; wilful omission or false declarations carry fraud penalties of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for a 12-month period; treaty rates of 0%, 5% or 10% may apply to non-EU shareholders depending on shareholding and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficiary must submit a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence jurisdiction to the Luxembourg paying agent before distribution, together with form 100-PS / Form 12, proof of shareholding period, and a beneficial-ownership statement. If tax is withheld at 15%, a reclaim must be lodged with the Administration des contributions directes within three years, appending TRC and complete documentation of economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest to non-residents. Treaty rates are generally 0% under most DTAs where beneficial ownership is proven; anti-abuse rules may recharacterise excessive, artificial or hybrid payments as constructive dividends subject to 15% withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CbCR/Master File obligation arises when the multinational group consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750 million; Luxembourg tax circulars additionally require Local File and TP documentation when annual controlled transactions exceed EUR 250,000; arm's-length benchmarking is mandatory for all related-party transactions in AI/LLM API licensing and token monetisation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not have a distinct ESR statute comparable to BVI/UAE, but ATAD, GAAR, and Administrative Circular LIR n° 56/1 require real staff, office, business decision-making, risk-taking capability, and economic substance to retain Luxembourg tax residence, treaty benefits, and transfer-pricing recognition. A letterbox SARL controlling AI/LLM token revenue without actual activity is exposed to treaty denial and recharacterisation of its seat.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent tax evasion and false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully under-declaring AI/LLM API token revenues, concealing USDC or cryptocurrency wallets, using fabricated invoices, or intentionally omitting beneficial owner information from the annual Form 100 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years per count; additional tax assessment of evaded tax plus interest at 2.6%; civil penalties between 20% and 200% of the evaded amount; loss of loss-carryforwards and all credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; criminal travel bans, asset freezes, and confiscation orders may be imposed; corporate veil may be pierced where the SARL is a mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / letterbox company without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL with no real office, no employees, and no decision-making substance, while all AI/LLM operations, token custody, and administration are carried out abroad; claiming Luxembourg treaty benefits as the principal purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the Luxembourg seat, reallocate profits to the jurisdiction of effective management, deny DTA benefits and treaty withholding relief, and assess 10% to 200% penalties, plus 15% dividend withholding on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers can be made personally liable for re-assessed tax, subject to personal bankruptcy, travel bans, and imprisonment up to three years in cases of intentional abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing and arm's-length abuse on AI APIs / USDC revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling LLM inference API services to a related offshore reseller at zero or manipulated margins, undervaluing USDC/token conversion, omitting the required Local File or benchmark study, or paying excessive royalties to a low-tax jurisdiction without real transfer of IP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustments restore the profit to arm's-length level; additional tax bears 5% monthly surcharge up to 20% plus 2.6% late interest; abusive adjustment is recharacterised as a constructive dividend subject to 15% withholding tax; criminal prosecution applies if false documentation is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer-pricing documentation or approve non-arm's-length intercompany agreements are liable in civil damages for the tax deficit; in agreement with fraud, personal criminal liability, travel bans and disqualification orders apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised profit repatriation through loans, royalties or cryptocurrency transfers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Extracting profits as inflated interest, artificial software license fees, or informal USDC transfers to shareholders without filing dividend withholding tax; structuring repayment of loans with no legal documentation or economic reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment is treated as a constructive dividend taxed at 15% Luxembourg withholding tax; non-payment triggers automatic penalties of 5% on the unpaid withholding tax per month, a fine up to EUR 1 million for serious failures, and possible criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company officers who fail to discharge withholding obligations become personally liable for the withheld amount; criminal imprisonment up to two years, travel bans, and civil restitution orders where intent and personal benefit are demonstrated.
